title: Exhibit c=6 floor words that keep the multiset (6,6,6,7,7,7).
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Constructive witness and an exhaustive census of two endpoint domains. No new κ, and the selected frontier stays `781451/250000000`.

In the unchanged unsigned dirty connector, one six-source characteristic-6 floor word keeps the diagonal sum `q_s + q_{39-s}` a permutation of `(6,6,6,7,7,7)` at every index `s = 4,...,18`. The same holds for every constant mask: 120 pure-slide words, one for each 3-subset of sources and each final letter. A second explicit word keeps the multiset while moving the mask from `{0,1,2}` at `s = 4` to `{0,1,4}` at `s = 5,...,18`.

Evidence class, stated separately:

1. **Exhaustive finite census** of the splits of this multiset at `s = 18` and at `s = 4`. The domains are finite, the loops visit every element, and the counts match the binomial closed forms in the README.
2. **Explicit construction** of the 120 constant-mask words, checked on every word.
3. **One constructive witness** for a chain whose mask moves. That witness is not a census of unequal-mask chains.

This is not a proof of the unrestricted six-source depth-two exclusion, which remains the solver verdict in merged PR #6141. No DRAT certificate is emitted. The joint exclusion under hypotheses (H1) and (H2) of open PR #7029 is unchanged: Lemma 1 forces `q_18` to be identically 3, so none of these words realizes the weight-3 shape at `(0, 9)`.

## Task and overlap

Base: CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`, re-fetched at session start and again before submission; both reads were that commit. Head: unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds `cursor/c6-t1-multiset-chain-bfc3` at `807149a85d185b8272aa1fda43ba6d8d7c541cfe`.

Task card: `connector-alphabet-change` (priority revision 8). Scope status: **changed**. The card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the alphabet fixed and answers open question 1 of PR #7029: whether splits of the type-T1 multiset `(6,6,6,7,7,7)` at `s = 4` and `s = 18` can sit in one monotone chain. A new operation is not the missing step. This is a side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or κ.

Package: `research/six-source-c6-t1-multiset-chain`.

Overlap was checked against open upstream PRs, including #7005–#7038, and against discussion #1166. A search for the multiset string hits PR #7029 and no other open upstream PR. Merged PR #6955 classifies the centre and is not repeated. PR #7029 classifies the six separation-3 families and prices `(0, 9)`; this package uses type T1 and does not recount those families. The `s + t = 15` shape question and the characteristic-5 remainders are different questions. Local overlap search of 10,178 notes on this base found no package answering this chain.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root. Author-checked on 2026-11-10 at head `807149a85d185b8272aa1fda43ba6d8d7c541cfe`:

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/six-source-c6-t1-multiset-chain/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/six-source-c6-t1-multiset-chain/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/six-source-c6-t1-multiset-chain
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/six-source-c6-t1-multiset-chain --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Marker: `PASS_SIX_SOURCE_C6_T1_MULTISET_CHAIN rows=4 splits18=20 splits4=120 domain4=756 constant_words=120 moving_mask_changes=1 controls=10`

The written argument is in the package README. The checker exhausts the legal local rows, the 20 type-T1 splits at `s = 18`, and all 756 pairs `(q_4, w_35)`. It evaluates all 120 constant-mask words and the moving word at every `s = 4,...,18`. It does not search depth-two words and does not rerun the SAT encoding. Both command modes, the registered package replay, and the commit-byte check passed. No Lean, Docker, or historical suite was run.

Hypotheses, stated exactly: `k = 6`, `c = 6`, floor words of length 36 calling each source six times, and `S(s) = q_s + q_{39-s}` having multiset `(6,6,6,7,7,7)` for every `s = 4,...,18`. The census is the finite set of count pairs at those two indices. It is not a census of all words, and it is not a census of unequal-mask chains.

## Credit

The depth-two interface and the weight identity are Nick Petalas's (PR #4231, PR #4248, PR #6107), with the Ross Richardson PR #934 / PR #943 lineage. JosieElliston's PR #6141 records the c=6 solver verdict. PR #6955 supplies the empty centre. PR #7029, head `8fe9a44a114efd4d3718208fd8f7c592fd03af62`, isolates type T1 and asks the question answered here. Nick Petalas's handoff on 2026-11-03 (discussion comment 19384981) states the diagonal slot count. The upstream finding for the open question is discussion comment 19514157.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Which endpoint pairs with unequal masks are joined by a monotone chain of `(6,6,6,7,7,7)`? Every equal-mask pair is realized here, and one unequal pair is realized by the moving word. First step: search the finite `(r, f)` graph for `M_4 = {0,1,2}`, `D = 3`, `M_18 = {3,4,5}`. The constant-mask proof uses equal early and late budgets, which fail as soon as the masks differ. A complete answer would still not be the unrestricted c=6 exclusion.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The equal early and late letter budgets are visible from the endpoint split before any search, and they are what make the constant-mask chain a pure slide.
